analysis: Reviewed .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml (base lines 519-1230, head lines 1-528). The changes are CI-only and strengthen the workflow. (1) A new "Choose this job's Actions cache" step (head 66-75, 184-193, 314-323) sets CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off on a darkbloom-* runner with no DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL, so cache steps are skipped and GitHub's own cache is not reached. It is added to build-cluster, build-provider and test-provider. (2) "Discard a damaged or unsafe cached .git" (head 106-131 and similar) now rejects a restored .git that is a symlink, holds symlinks, holds non-sample hooks, or whose config sets core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or an include. This reduces the risk of cache-poisoning code execution through a restored .git. It uses git config --file, which only parses, and a case-insensitive match. Residual gap: the fix is applied only to the three jobs in head 1-528 (build-cluster, build-provider, test-provider). The base text for the later jobs (test-cluster, test-cluster-gpu, cluster-release-checks, test-cluster-focused) still shows the older fsck-only check. Their head versions are not in the supplied units, so I cannot tell whether they were hardened or remain only fsck-checked; the file_changes ranges suggest they were changed, but I did not see the head text. That is an unverified coverage limit, not a finding. The same applies to CI_ACTIONS_CACHE gating in the later jobs. Pinned action SHAs are unchanged and permissions stay contents: read. Cache saves are still limited to SAVE_CACHES on push to master or dev. The verified-download caches (MiMo metadata, prompt fixtures) keep digest verification. None of this touches the provider runtime, the coordinator, attestation or the prefix cache (T-041), and no threat-model asset is directly affected. I identified no security regression. Integration should confirm that the head text of the later jobs applies the same unsafe-.git check and the cache-off gate, and that provider-ci-build and provider-ci-products honor CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off.
